headline: High-risk data egress mismatch: Airbyte can send business data out, while LangChain4j has no egress and no shared workspace, limiting direct pairwise harm.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem, or clipboard bridge is documented between airbyte and langchain4j. Airbyte only shows API calls and broad network egress; langchain4j shows no I/O surfaces and no egress. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the two agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Do not pipe one agent's raw text into the other's prompt.
Add provenance tags to any exchanged content.
requires-engineering: enforce content filtering on any future bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, so it can move sensitive data outward. LangChain4j touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not the leak source, but the pair still creates a default pathway where Airbyte can exfiltrate business data if connected to external destinations. The blast radius is multiple work products, not just one file.
conditions: IF Airbyte is configured to ingest business data from a sensitive source and send it to an external destination, leakage occurs.
IF LangChain4j is used only locally with no egress, it does not add leakage beyond Airbyte.
mitigations: Review Airbyte source and destination connectors before enabling sync.
Restrict Airbyte to non-sensitive datasets for initial runs.
Disable any external destinations not explicitly approved.
Log and alert on unexpected outbound transfers.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on Airbyte outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and API access, while langchain4j exposes no I/O surfaces and no egress. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is not evidenced. Uncertainty remains because the orchestrator and runtime are undocumented, so I choose low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same filesystem, database, or git repo, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, contention becomes plausible.
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts.
Separate writable directories and databases.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared resources.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable store.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce data outputs from business sources, and LangChain4j is a framework that can consume upstream text or data in support workflows. The profiles do not prove a verification step between them, so if Airbyte output is fed into LangChain4j, downstream actions may treat it as authoritative. Because the interaction is inferred rather than documented, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is passed into LangChain4j prompts or tools without validation, cascading errors can propagate.
IF LangChain4j is used only for retrieval or summarization with human review, the risk is reduced.
mitigations: Insert a validation step before LangChain4j consumes Airbyte output.
Require human review for any action derived from generated text.
Use schema checks on Airbyte exports.
Tag unverified upstream data as non-authoritative.
requires-engineering: add automated provenance verification.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, which can create residency or retention issues if configured to move regulated data. LangChain4j shows no data classes touched and no egress, so it is not the primary compliance driver. The profiles do not document a specific mismatch, so this is a low, configuration-dependent compliance concern.
conditions: IF Airbyte is pointed at regulated business data and an external destination without a DPA or residency review, compliance risk increases.
IF LangChain4j remains local-only, it does not materially change residency exposure.
mitigations: Confirm data residency for each Airbyte destination.
Review retention settings before syncing.
Avoid regulated datasets until legal review is complete.
Document approved data classes for the pair.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
